readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckLocalization.cutoff_hasFDerivAt_two
readback.mathematical_statement: Use the fixed real Euclidean E=ClosedSmoothModel 3=EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), Bilin=E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R, Jet1=E ->L[R] Bilin, and Jet2=E ->L[R] Jet1, with the original Euclidean norm and nested continuous-linear-map operator norms. The literal four letI binders install the canonical ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedAddCommGroup and toNormedSpace dictionaries, with scalar and semilinear fields all R and RingHom.id R. No alternative norm, equivalent renorming, free dictionary, tensor symmetry restriction or altered scalar action is quantified. The pinned Variables uses its existing nested maximum product norm. The also-pinned parabolic Y retains its value-sup plus scaled-difference-sup sum norm, Graph retains the u,ut,du,ddu Y sum norm and genuine derivative certificates, and nine-entry Inputs retains the original finite Pi maximum norm. None of alpha,T,Y,Graph or Inputs occurs as a quantified input or bound in this declaration. For every total scalar function chi:E -> R, total Bilin-valued function f:E -> Bilin, field J:E -> Jet1, H:Jet2, and z:E, assume exactly: chi is globally ContDiff R 2; for every y:E, HasFDerivAt f (J y) y; and HasFDerivAt J H z. No global C2 premise on f or global C1 premise on J, compact support of chi/f, chosen cutoff-one neighborhood, symmetry premise, supplied product derivative, metric, background, invertibility or flow premise is added. The all-y derivative premise identifies J(y)=fderiv R f y everywhere, by uniqueness of the actual ambient Frechet derivative. The final premise therefore certifies H=fderiv R (fderiv R f) z as the derivative of that actual first-derivative field at z; J is not merely a formal pointwise jet with an unspecified neighborhood. Write c=chi(z), dc=fderiv R chi z, ddc=fderiv R (fderiv R chi) z, h=f(z), and j=J(z). The global C2 premise supplies the actual derivatives dc and ddc, where ddc:E ->L[R] E ->L[R] R is exactly the Bilin type. With g(y)=chi(y) smul f(y), the conclusion is a conjunction of two actual ambient derivative certificates at the same z. First, HasFDerivAt g (cutoffFirst c dc h j) z, with cutoffFirst(c,dc,h,j)(u)=c smul j(u)+dc(u) smul h. Second, HasFDerivAt (y |-> fderiv R g y) (cutoffSecond c dc ddc h j H) z. The differentiated function in this second certificate is the actual first fderiv field of the product on all E, not J, a separately supplied product-jet field, or a pointwise surrogate. The all-y derivative premise and the C2 chi premise allow the first product formula to identify this actual product fderiv at every y before its derivative at z is taken. For arbitrary ordered directions u,v:E, the pinned second derivative evaluates to c smul H(u)(v)+dc(u) smul j(v)+dc(v) smul j(u)+ddc(u)(v) smul h. In cutoffSecond, dc.smulRight J contributes dc(u) smul j(v); smulRightL.precompR E dc J contributes dc(v) smul j(u); and smulRightL.precompL E ddc h contributes ddc(u)(v) smul h. Both ordered mixed terms and the actual cutoff Hessian term are retained, with no implicit replacement by one mixed term or appeal to unassumed symmetry. By the two HasFDerivAt certificates, the formula also identifies the actual first fderiv of g at z and the actual second fderiv fderiv R (fderiv R g) z. This conditional product-rule theorem proves exactly these two local certificates from the stated global first-derivative identification and the second-derivative certificate at z. It does not assert existence of chi,f,J,H satisfying an external metric/Graph germ, construct a cutoff, establish boundedness/Holder estimates or nonlinear coordinate covariance, or identify an arbitrary formal H without the last premise. No missing product term, false derivative-field premise or norm substitution was found.
